messages:
sara-cs: Heads-up — Cedarwood (tenant cedarwood-31) opened a P1: search UI timeouts. They report p95 around 2.4s and p99 up to 6s for embeddings calls starting ~03:15 UTC. Customer impact: web search blocked. Screenshot + logs attached by customer: https://files.internal/cedarwood/latency-0315.png. Can someone triage? @maya-eng @tom-sre

maya-eng: On it. Quick questions: which model/route are they hitting? qps pattern? any recent deploys to the embedding pool?

sara-cs: They call /v1/embeddings with model=text-embed-2 and route=shared-embeds-prod. qps baseline 25, spikes to ~110 during their batch jobs (they run hourly). No deploys from Cedarwood this hour per audit.

tom-sre: Pulling metrics now. Running:
```
redwoodctl metrics query --tenant cedarwood-31 --metric latency.p95,latency.p99,request.qps --window 60m --granularity 1m
```
Prelim output (last 30m):
- p95: 1.2s -> 2.6s (sharp jump at 03:12)
- p99: 2.1s -> 6.3s
- qps: 28 steady, spikes to 115 at 03:11
Also seeing increased queuing on shared-embeds-prod pool.

ops-bot: Alert: tenant cedarwood-31 breached concurrency threshold (threshold=50) at 03:11:42 UTC — automatic soft-throttle applied.

maya-eng: That soft-throttle explains some 429s/timeouts. But p99 at 6s suggests requests are waiting for GPU availability then timing out. Could be noisy neighbor (large batch job from another tenant) or large single requests with long sequences. Can we get a sample of request sizes?

tom-sre: Querying request payload sizes:
```
redwoodctl logs search --tenant cedarwood-31 --service embeddings --since 03:00 --tail 200 | jq '.payload_length' | sort | uniq -c | tail
```
Result: most are small (~64 tokens) but ~10% are big batches (5k tokens) clustered at 03:10-03:12. Also see another tenant (tenant: pineview-9) with heavy batched requests at same time. Looks like contention in the shared pool.

jack-ml: Noted: long contexts cause KV cache misses and can blow up per-request memory/time. If both tenants hit the same model variant, kernel selection may be suboptimal for mixed seq lengths.

eli-platform: Immediate mitigation options:
1) Move Cedarwood to a quieter reserved pool (hotfix) — takes ~5-10min to route.
2) Apply stricter per-tenant concurrency cap (lower than soft-throttle) to smooth bursts: `tenant-config set cedarwood-31 concurrency_limit=20`.
3) Temporarily allowlist Cedarwood for high-priority routing to reserved-pool-8: `route override --tenant cedarwood-31 --pool reserved-pool-8 --ttl 1h`.
Which one do we want to try first?

sara-cs: Customer asking for fastest resolution. They prefer not to move pools if possible. They asked for an allowlist so their UI stays snappy during business hours.

maya-eng: Let's start with (2) to stop their bursts, and (3) as a fallback if p99 doesn't improve. I'll apply concurrency_limit=20 now and watch. Command below:
```
redwoodctl tenant-config set --tenant cedarwood-31 --key concurrency_limit --value 20
```
Applying...

deploy-bot: tenant-config updated: cedarwood-31 concurrency_limit=20 by maya-eng at 03:26 UTC.

tom-sre: Metrics 5m after change:
- p95: 2.6s -> 1.05s
- p99: 6.3s -> 1.8s
- qps: spikes capped ~40
Looks much better. Customer still sees occasional 2s outliers when other tenants spike.

jack-ml: For longer-term stability we should advise Cedarwood to avoid hourly large batch runs during peak shared-pool times or schedule them into a dedicated reservation. Also recommend enabling prefix/KV caching for their common prompts — sample config:
```
route-config {
  embeddings: {
    kv_cache: enabled,
    cache_ttl: 3600
  }
}
```
This will reduce compute for repeated prefixes.

maya-eng: Customer asked for a permanent option: Can we create a small reserved slot for them (1 GPU) as a paid add-on? Eli — can you draft cost/lead time?

eli-platform: Yes. Reserving a 1xA10G -> provisioning & routing change ~15-20min. Estimate: $X/month. I'll open a sales ticket and provision a trial reserved-pool for 24h so they can validate.

sara-cs: Cedarwood accepted the temporary concurrency cap and will test for the next 2 hours. They also requested an allowlist for their internal batch job host so it can use the reserved slot if available, otherwise fall back to shared. Is that doable?

eli-platform: Yep — we can add their job runner IP -> tenant mapping and add a routing policy:
```
route-policy add --name cedarwood-batch-priority --match ip:10.22.7.18 --tenant cedarwood-31 --prefer reserved-pool-8 --fallback shared-embeds-prod
```
I'll apply after we confirm reserved pool readiness.

tom-sre: Follow-up checks: I also saw a node in shared-embeds-prod with elevated CPU jitter during the spike. Filing a postmortem item to investigate kernel scheduling for mixed batch sizes — tagging eng-runtime.

ops-bot: NOTE: incident created: INC-2026-0456 "Cedarwood shared-pool contention" assigned to eng-runtime.

maya-eng: Summary for slack updates and CS reply:
- Cause: simultaneous large batched requests from multiple tenants caused queueing in shared-embeds-prod -> high p95/p99 for Cedarwood.
- Immediate mitigation: applied per-tenant concurrency_limit=20 (reduced p95/p99 immediately). Reserved-pool trial & routing allowlist being provisioned for higher SLO.
- Next steps: recommend customer spread batch jobs or use reserved pool; eng-runtime to investigate scheduling/kernel path for mixed seq-length workloads.

sara-cs: I'll send this to Cedarwood and keep thread open until reserved pool trial completes. Thanks all. :pray:

(10:00 UTC later) maya-eng: Reserved-pool-8 provisioned and routing allowlist applied for cedarwood-31 for 24h trial. Quick smoke metrics show p95 ~120ms, p99 ~240ms for their baseline traffic.

sara-cs: Customer verified UI is responsive again and gave thumbs-up. Closing P1 after they confirm 2h stable.

jack-ml: Logging note: add an opt-in ticket to enable kv_cache for Cedarwood route; will coordinate with DE to create a config toggle and docs for customers.

tom-sre: Postmortem item created; will include mitigation timeline and suggested operator tools (tenant-level traffic shaping, improved per-pool isolation).

sara-cs: Closing thread — final status: mitigated via concurrency cap + reserved pool trial; customer satisfied.
